column1: Aerospace costing checklist (from the Emithran aerospace should-cost guide)

Part A: the checks to run on any aerospace should-cost or quote. Part B: a build-up pre-filled with the titanium bracket example. Part C: a forging vs machining break-even calculator - all figures illustrative, replace with your own.
Material: Price is for the certified, traceable specification you require - not a commercial grade
Material: Stock form and size match what the supplier will actually buy (plate, bar, forging, casting)
Material: Buy-to-fly ratio calculated from your drawing and stock size
Material: Chip / scrap recovery value included at a realistic rate
Material: Material price is dated, and an index is agreed for the LTA
Material: Certification and testing (mill certs, test reports, traceability) costed
Special processes: Full routing listed from the drawing and customer specification
Special processes: Minimum-lot charges per process captured, and the lot size they cover
Special processes: Transport to and from processors, and waiting time, included
Special processes: Supplier handling markup on subcontracted processes identified
Quality: First article inspection costed (one-off and per batch)
Quality: Per-part inspection of key characteristics (e.g. CMM time) costed
Quality: Quality system, audits and records sit in rates or overhead - not counted twice
Quality: Scrap and rework allowance reflects late-routing rejection risk
Volume: Batch size and release pattern stated; quotes compared at the same batch size
Volume: Price breaks requested at several batch sizes
Volume: One-off costs (programming, FAI, dies, fixtures) spread over the stated programme quantity
Rates: Machine and labour rates fit the supplier’s location and machine type
RFQ: Cost breakdown requested in a standard template (stock, cycle time, setup, processes, inspection, margin)
RFQ: Certification, approval and documentation requirements stated up front
LTA: Volume bands and batch-size price breaks agreed
LTA: Material element indexed to an agreed index and the stock weight
LTA: Productivity / cycle-time improvement sharing agreed
LTA: Tooling, die and fixture ownership agreed, including on change of supplier
LTA: Scheduled should-cost refresh and review triggers agreed
